data.completion_memo: Implemented Dependency View mode for the Design Browser. Added a Branch/Dependency segmented control for C4 views, deterministic branch-neighborhood projection from C4 elements and relationships, incoming/core/outgoing layout roles, capped relationship inclusion for dense branches, generated dependency projection source details, and Structurizr view-level relationship records so arrows and labels render reliably. Preserved existing branch C4 and UML artifact behavior. Verified with cargo fmt, cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri\Cargo.toml, cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri\Cargo.toml, npm run build outside the sandbox after the known esbuild EPERM, git diff --check, and a local Structurizr smoke render of the Adashi MCP branch showing external store/runtime dependencies and relationship labels.

lines:
Implement the relation-aware Dependency View mode from the formal design.

Acceptance criteria:
- Add a Design Browser view mode/control for switching from the current branch C4 projection to Dependency View.
- Build a deterministic branch-neighborhood projection from formal C4 elements and relationships: selected branch children plus immediate incoming/outgoing dependency endpoints outside the branch.
- Keep the formal C4/UML model as source of truth; do not introduce freehand diagram edits or AI-invented layout state.
- Rank/layer nodes by containment and dependency direction so the diagram is readable and stable.
- Show key relationship labels and technology/protocol text while keeping full detail available through the inspector/source panels.
- Limit or group low-priority/noisy edges so dense branches do not collapse into unreadable spaghetti.
- Preserve existing branch-scoped browser behavior and typed UML artifact tabs.
- Verify with Rust checks/tests where relevant, frontend build, and a visual/manual check of a branch with real relationships such as the MCP server or Design Browser branch.

data.title: Implement Dependency View mode for Design Browser
